loop.what: v4, 148.04-159.11 s (the twelve shouts) and, clean, the EXECUTION plate of chorus 1 (69.34 s). One small program instead of v3's twelve regenerate attempts. The listing itself is code and lives in src/scenes/loop.js; this entry is its record.
loop.why: The loop condition is the request the client refused (illegal_request): the same person, the same word. `love` is the value the persona card left undefined at boot. Line 07 is the only line that matters, and with the user gone it is never reached. In chorus 1 the user is online, so the loop is never entered and line 07 runs: what it says goes to them.
loop.syllables: The sung word is four even syllables (beats N, N+0.5, N+1, N+1.5 of each two-beat round). They are the four statements of the loop body, lines 02-05: the execution bar moves down one line per syllable, and the big word at the bottom right is printed solid in four blocks (character ranges 0-2, 2-3, 3-5, 5-9).
loop.seen: One composition for all twelve rounds, on the dark ground of the error state: the listing top left with the three red tags at the ends of lines 02-04 (the same three every round), a round counter with no total and a cream `stop` key (`yours`) that nobody presses bottom left, the arrow from line 06 back to 01 lighting at every turn, and the output bottom right: the word of the round in progress, always in the same place, and every finished round pushed up above it as one more step of a staircase. The picture changes only three times, each the same composition enlarged: round 5 (151.73 s), round 9 (155.42 s), and round 12 (158.19 s), where the word takes the whole frame, torn along one horizontal cut into two halves out of register, the staircase leaves by the top and the counter overflows. From round 9 on, one tear a round.

count_moves.what: v4, 159.11-161.88 s. One card per number, ON the beat it is sung on (global beats 344-349). The loop is interrupted (^C) and the same call is tried in six languages. Six moves of one family (a terminal's own), each finished within 0.12 s; the frame stays dark throughout.
count_moves.fixed: On all six cards, in the same place: top left `^C` and `> for (lang of [de, es, fr, ko, sv, zh]) say(love, lang);` with the current language lit and the ones already said struck out; beside the numeral the call `say(love, "<the language's own name>")`; bottom centre `replies 0 / n`, where n grows with every card and the 0 is red and never changes.

moves.move: Cursor drop: the card is printed behind a bar that falls from the top of the frame to the bottom, cubic ease-out, 0.10 s.
Newline: the outgoing card travels up by one frame height while the incoming one follows from below, locked together, cubic ease-out, 0.12 s; the numeral trails three ghost samples.
Carriage return: the incoming card is revealed from the right edge to the left behind a vertical bar, cubic ease-out, 0.10 s.
Column print: sixteen columns 120 px wide, each printed top to bottom in 0.06 s, column i starting i x 4 ms after the cut; done at 0.12 s.
Punch-in: hard cut; only the numeral arrives at 160 % and settles to 100 % in 0.10 s (exponential), its two previous frames left as ghosts.
Row interleave: nine rows 120 px tall, even rows from the left and odd rows from the right, cubic ease-out, 0.12 s.

final_shout.seen: v4, 161.88-162.81 s. Not code: for the only time in this stretch the word is in her serif, in two rows that fill the frame (its first five letters, three syllables; its last four, the fourth). Every letter is a window onto her face (f_eye, mirrored, at the registration the next section opens on). The four syllables light the four groups of letters; on the fourth her open eye is there in the stem of the second letter of the lower row, and holds to the cut.
final_shout.rules: It only gets brighter: no fade to black, no flash. A face is in the frame, so nothing tears and no transition warps it.
